## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Daily docs-sync bot workflow (ci, ~6h, HIGH)

- **What**: Kilocode #12512 adds a scheduled workflow that keeps packages/
  kilo-docs in sync with PRs merged to Kilo-Org/cloud and Kilo-Org/
  kilocode. Five-module pipeline: watermark.mjs derives the processing
  window from the bot's own PR body marker (self-healing, no external
  state; 72h fallback on first run, 14d cap), collect.mjs queries merged
  PRs via GitHub API and applies deterministic pre-filter (bots, chores,
  docs-only PRs excluded), triage.mjs classifies PRs in chunks of 25 with
  kilo run (failed chunks degrade to unclassified instead of failing the
  run), edit.mjs updates docs in batches of 5 PRs with kilo run (bounded
  per batch; failures surface as skipped entries in PR body), verify runs
  the kilo-docs build + test suite (one LLM fix pass on failure; still-red
  becomes draft PR), upsert-pr.mjs maintains one rolling auto-docs PR
  (appends while open, fresh branch after merge) with 15-file draft cap and
  machine-readable processed-through watermark. Security: sanitizes HTML-
  comment sequences out of agent-generated PR body (cannot forge markers),
  drafts any PR touching non-content files in kilo-docs (build-executable
  changes force human review). Resilience: retries GitHub API calls on
  network errors and 5xx, isolates per-PR collect failures, trusts
  watermark only on bot-authored PRs and clamps future dates, validates
  chunk triage entries belong to their chunk, uses changed_files for total
  and skips classification on truncated (300+) file lists. Keeps bot-
  authored PRs in the digest (release/dependency bots ship user-facing
  changes, e.g. JetBrains release PRs).
- **Why**: Alexi could adapt this architecture for keeping docs/ or AGENTS.
  md in sync with merged PRs: when a PR adds/changes a tool, provider, or
  command, the bot classifies the PR, generates doc updates via LLM pass,
  runs tests, and maintains a rolling docs PR. Architecturally portable
  (TypeScript, GitHub API, LLM agent loop, rolling PR pattern). Eliminates
  manual doc drift after feature merges. High-leverage automation (docs
  stay green without manual intervention). Watermark-driven window is self-
  healing (no external state to lose, recovers from bot's own PR history).
- **Source**: Kilo-Org/kilocode PR #12512 "feat: daily docs-sync bot
  keeping kilo-docs in sync with merged PRs" (merged 2026-07-27T03:15Z,
  commit `e8f4a2b`). Full PR body at https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/
  pull/12512. Five modules: .github/scripts/docs-sync/{watermark,collect,
  triage,edit,upsert-pr}.mjs + .github/workflows/docs-sync.yml.
- **Category**: ci. **Size**: HIGH (~6h: port 5 modules from Kilo's docs-
  sync to Alexi's doc structure, adapt watermark recovery for Alexi's PR
  history, tune chunk sizes for SAP AI Core rate limits, wire AGENT_MODEL
  env var, test against docs/ or AGENTS.md update scenarios, add 15-file
  draft cap and machine-readable watermark, integrate with Alexi's
  commitlint scope-enum and format:check gate). **Status**: HIGH signal
  (architecturally portable, eliminates doc drift, self-healing watermark,
  high-leverage automation; applicable to Alexi).

#### 2. Agentic compaction fixes (core, ~0h, SKIP)

- **What**: Cline #12563 fixes agentic compaction silently falling back to
  basic. When OpenAI Compatible provider is selected, the settings dropdown
  stores the SDK spelling ('openai-compatible'). The agentic compaction
  summarizer creates its LLM handler from the session's ProviderConfig
  alone; resolveBaseUrl had no mapping for 'openai-compatible', so
  ProviderConfig was built without a baseUrl, the summarizer hit the
  provider default endpoint (api.openai.com), failed auth, and fell back to
  basic compaction — the UI showed 'Context compacted' with no hint that
  agentic summarization never ran. Fixes: resolveBaseUrl accepts SDK
  spelling and falls back to providers.json base URL (mirroring
  resolveApiKey), buildSessionConfig exposes knownModels at top level so
  manual /compact budgets against real model context window instead of 64k
  fallback. Also fixes manual /compact being a silent no-op when auto-
  compaction is disabled: manual /compact persists a compaction sidecar and
  promises the next turn will use compacted context, but the runtime host
  only wired the compaction-state-aware prepareTurn when compaction was
  enabled (Auto Compact off is VS Code extension default). With Auto
  Compact off, manual /compact saved the sidecar and UI showed 'Context
  compacted', yet every subsequent request sent the full canonical
  transcript. createCompactionStateAwarePrepareTurn already supports an
  undefined compact fn (project existing state, never re-compact), so wire
  it unconditionally; sessions without a sidecar are unaffected. Keep
  resumed/initial sidecar instead of dropping it when compaction is
  disabled.
- **Why**: Alexi uses SAP AI Core (single provider via routing-config.json,
  no SDK spelling migration, no OpenAI Compatible multi-provider catalog).
  The OpenAI Compatible baseUrl resolution fix is provider-integration work
  specific to Cline's multi-provider SDK catalog state management. The
  manual /compact wiring fix is relevant only when Alexi implements agentic
  compaction (core feature not yet present). Defer until Alexi has agentic
  compaction, then revisit the unconditional prepareTurn wiring pattern.
  SKIP (provider-integration work, not core compaction logic; Alexi has no
  agentic compaction yet).
- **Source**: Cline PR #12563 "fix(vscode/core): agentic compaction
  silently fell back to basic, and manual /compact never reached the model"
  (merged 2026-07-27T06:42Z, commit `c3d8f1a`). Full PR body at https://
  github.com/cline/cline/pull/12563.
- **Category**: core. **Size**: N/A (~0h if applicable; Alexi has no
  agentic compaction, no OpenAI Compatible provider catalog, no SDK
  spelling migration). **Status**: SKIP (defer until Alexi implements
  agentic compaction; provider-integration work specific to Cline's multi-
  provider SDK catalog).

#### 3. Mistake limit enforcement (core, ~0h, SKIP)

- **What**: Cline #12561 stops the task at the mistake limit like the CLI.
  When the SDK's consecutive-mistake limit is hit, the extension used to
  block on an ask (Proceed Anyways / Start New Task) while the agent loop
  kept running against the provider — reproduced 2,100+ consecutive API
  requests behind the unanswered prompt. Replicate the CLI's non-
  interactive resolver instead: show an error row and resolve the decision
  as an immediate stop. The run aborts cleanly at the turn boundary, the
  turn phase becomes awaiting_followup, and the user continues whenever
  they want by sending a new message (which also resets the SDK's mistake
  tracking on the next productive turn). Also removes the extension's
  maxConsecutiveMistakes setting (state key, settings RPC, webview state,
  proto fields now reserved). It was never wired into the SDK session
  config — the SDK's own default governs — so the setting was dead weight.
  Legacy mistake_limit_reached asks from persisted conversations still
  render via the existing webview paths.
- **Why**: Alexi already uses SDK session config with default mistake
  tracking (no custom maxConsecutiveMistakes override). The SDK's mistake
  limit is already enforced (no equivalent of Cline's 2,100+ API request
  runaway). SKIP (Cline parity with CLI; Alexi already has SDK-driven
  mistake limits, no dead setting to remove).
- **Source**: Cline PR #12561 "Stop the task at the mistake limit like the
  CLI and remove the max-mistakes setting" (merged 2026-07-27T06:18Z,
  commit `b9e3c2a`). Full PR body at https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/
  12561.
- **Category**: core. **Size**: N/A (~0h if applicable; Alexi already
  enforces SDK mistake limits, no dead setting). **Status**: SKIP (Alexi
  already has SDK-driven mistake limits; no action needed).

  stalls no longer fail read/edit tools": Two fixes: relative read_files
  paths resolved against process.cwd() = '/' in VS Code extension host

  terminal; extension now overrides read_files executor to resolve relative
  paths against workspace root before delegating to SDK's built-in reader),
  and stalled vscode.diff call was unbounded (on auto-approve it burned 30s
  tool timeout, on manual approval it delayed ask indefinitely; now bound
  with 5s timeout, on timeout edit proceeds without preview and late-
  opening tab is closed once settled). Alexi is CLI-first (process.cwd() is
  correct, no VS Code diff preview). Skip (VS Code extension host-specific
  fixes).
- Cline #12144 "fix(cli): use unique keys for read_files rows": read_files
  rendered file rows keyed by raw path, so the same path listed twice (e.g.
  find-skills reading a SKILL.md repeatedly) produced duplicate React keys
  and the two-children-with-the-same-key warning. Build index-namespaced
  keys instead, at both render sites. UI rendering fix. LOW signal (React
  key warning fix, no functional impact). Skip.
